Market Patterns Work and Jeffrey Hirsch Explains Why | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 56

Jeffrey Hirsch presents seasonal market rules, including the midterm cycle, winter strength, January signals and sector windows. Eisman accepts parts of the framework while asking for causal explanations. The audit preserves the guest's explicit warnings about unstable signals, small Bitcoin samples and combining disciplines. Statistical claims remain unresolved without the original tests. Eisman's supporting assertions about a universal mutual-fund cash ceiling and nearly all credit growth occurring outside banks are contradicted by primary filings and Fed tables.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

How he reasons here

  • Distinguish executable fixed-window strategies from ex-post low-to-high returns.
  • Compare conditional success rates with the market's unconditional upward bias.
  • Retire failed signals and preserve out-of-sample tests.
  • Combine seasonality with fundamentals, technicals, policy and sentiment.
  • Do not turn a historical average into a dated target.
